# Auto Ontology Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own. It enables developers to: - Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer. - Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. - Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question. ## Benchmarks To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to [auto-ontology-eval](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval), which scores the same model with and without the ontology on [NeMo Gym](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym). > **Licensing & contributions.** Auto Ontology is distributed under the > [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Third-party open-source components > bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in > [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). **This project > is currently not accepting external contributions.** ## Key Features - **Natural-language querying** of structured data — questions are translated to SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM. - **Semantic catalog / ontology layer** over relational sources, stored in Postgres alongside the catalog it describes. - **Authentication & RBAC** —using [Better Auth](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth). - **Web UI** for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings. - **Flexible deployment** — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a local stack. ## Software Components | Component | Technology | Role | Default port | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------ | | Frontend | Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion worker | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings | 3002 | | Postgres + pgvector | Relational Database | App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Secure storage of connection credentials | — | ### NVIDIA NIM Auto Ontology uses NVIDIA NIM endpoints for inference — either the hosted [NVIDIA API catalog](https://build.nvidia.com) (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`) or self-hosted NIMs. The defaults in `.env.example` are: - **LLM:** `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` - **Embeddings:** `nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b` - **Reranking:** `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` The endpoints and models are configured via the `DEFAULT_MODELS_ENDPOINT`, `DEFAULT_MODELS_MODEL`, `EMBED_ENDPOINT`, and `EMBED_MODEL` environment variables and require a `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. #### Model triplets Each model role is configured by a **triplet** of environment variables — `_ENDPOINT` (URL), `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`: | Prefix | Role | | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `DEFAULT_MODELS` | Shared default; every field below falls back to it. | | `REASONING` | Main chat / NL-to-SQL model. | | `NON_REASONING` | Lighter model used for entity extraction. | | `EMBED` | Text-embedding model (must match between ingest and query). | | `RERANK` | Reranker used to build bridge-table SQL attributes. | You can set a full triplet, only some of its fields, or none at all — any field left unset falls back to the matching `DEFAULT_MODELS_`. So the simplest setup is to fill in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and override per-triplet fields only where they differ (e.g. `EMBED_MODEL`, `NON_REASONING_MODEL`). `*_API_KEY` also falls back to the legacy `NVIDIA_API_KEY` for backward compatibility. ## Quickstart This runs Auto-Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com). 1. Clone the repository and create `.env`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology cp .env.example .env ``` Then set these values in `.env`: ```dotenv DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-... AUTH_SECRET= APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD= PGADMIN_PASSWORD= ``` Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. 2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set: ```bash docker compose up -d --wait postgres git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \ POSTGRES_PASSWORD='' \ uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop) ``` 3. Build and start the rest of the stack: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` 4. Open and sign in with `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Go to **Settings → Semantic Compilation** and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports **Semantic compilation is ready** when it finishes. 5. Ask a question in **Chat**: > What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania > in June 2015? The agent resolves *revenue*, *product*, and *state* to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source: ```text Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines. SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines FROM sales.invoicelines il JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll' AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania' AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01' Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province Validated the filter values against the data, then executed ``` 6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through [MCP](#mcp-server) checks answerability first and asks you to clarify: ```text You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015? Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend" Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another source I should connect? ``` If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for `localhost:3000` and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the [setup skill's troubleshooting guide](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/references/troubleshooting.md). ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph clients["Clients"] direction TB ui["Browser: web UI"] rest["Scripts: REST API with API tokens"] mcpc["MCP clients: Cursor, Claude Desktop, agents"] end mcp["MCP server: read-only tools (FastMCP, port 3003)"] fe["Web app, auth, API gateway (Next.js, port 3000)"] subgraph private["Private network"] direction TB be["Backend: text-to-SQL agent, catalog and ontology APIs (FastAPI, port 3001)"] ing["Ingestion and semantic compilation (FastAPI, port 3002)"] pg[("Postgres + pgvector: app data, catalog, ontology, embeddings")] end src[("Source databases: 10 connectors")] models["Model endpoints: NVIDIA NIM or OpenAI-compatible (reasoning, non-reasoning, embed, rerank)"] vault["Vault (optional): connection credentials"] kumo["KumoRFM (optional): predictions"] ui --> fe rest --> fe mcpc --> mcp mcp -- "public API" --> fe fe --> be fe -- "users, sessions, settings" --> pg be -- "trigger ingest and compile" --> ing be --> pg ing --> pg be -- "run SQL" --> src ing -- "read schema, sample values" --> src be --> models ing --> models be -.-> vault ing -.-> vault be -.-> kumo ``` Browser and API clients reach Auto-Ontology through the web app on port 3000. MCP clients connect to the MCP server on port 3003, which calls that same public API. Full pipeline detail, with tool-flow diagrams for generating an ontology and answering a question: [docs/architecture.md](./docs/architecture.md). Auto-Ontology works in two stages: it generates an ontology that people certify, and the agent answers questions from it. The ontology holds three kinds of definition: - **Terms.** Business concepts such as *Customer* or *Invoice Line*, each with a description and synonyms, mapped to the columns that hold them. - **SQL attributes.** Reviewed SQL expressions under a term, such as a margin or a rolling total. The agent reuses them, so answers compute each measure the same way. - **Relationships.** How tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from keys and from the data. **Generate.** The ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases, and people refine it. Semantic compilation starts once you turn it on in **Settings → Semantic Compilation**. - **Catalog ingest:** read tables, columns, keys, views, and query history; tag PII if you turn on PII detection; embed tables and columns in pgvector. - **Per table:** profile values with SQL. A model finds foreign key candidates and junction tables, writes column descriptions, and names the terms. - **Across tables:** group copies of a schema into term families, and link foreign keys to the terms they reference, keeping an inferred link only when the data confirms it. A model attaches foreign key columns left unlinked, suggests SQL attributes from query history and for bridge tables, and describes each column attribute. - **Output:** the ontology in Postgres with embeddings in pgvector, which you can import or export as Ossie YAML. - **Certify:** test the draft with real questions in Chat, or with `check_answerable` and `ask_question` over MCP. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API, and certify them once they're correct. Edits are re-embedded right away, and the next compilation keeps them, except which semantic foreign key each join uses, which every compilation re-selects. The [Generate tool flow](./docs/architecture.md#generate-an-ontology) shows which steps call a model and which are SQL or rules. The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting **Order** shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

**Answer.** The agent runs the same steps for every question: - **Classify:** a model labels the intent and separates any evidence written into the question. - **Retrieve:** embedding search finds candidate terms, columns, and SQL attributes, and a model keeps the relevant ones. - **Join:** join paths come from the ontology's semantic foreign keys, with no model involved. - **Write:** the reasoning model writes SQL and a plain-language explanation. - **Check and repair:** static checks and a model judge review the SQL. A rejected or failing query is repaired, and an empty result triggers a probe of the filter values. - **Answer:** the answer comes back with its SQL and the steps it took, and a chart in Chat. If no valid query comes out, the agent reports that the question can't be answered from this data. Predictive questions go to KumoRFM when `KUMO_RFM_API_URL` is set (see [Predictions](#predictions)). The [Answer tool flow](./docs/architecture.md#answer-a-question) shows every step, with the model or SQL each one uses. In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as CSV, or read them as a chart:

Auto-Ontology is compatible with [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/), the open standard for exchanging semantic models. Ossie includes a [converter for Auto-Ontology](https://github.com/apache/ossie-converters/tree/main/nvidia), which Auto-Ontology uses to import and export model definitions as Ossie YAML. Use **Settings → Import / Export**, or `POST /api/model/import` and `POST /api/model/export`. | Component | Technology | Role | Port | | ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---- | | Frontend | Next.js, Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, public API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Text-to-SQL agent, catalog, ontology APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion service | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingestion and semantic compilation | 3002 | | MCP server | FastMCP | Read-only agent tools over the public API | 3003 | | Postgres + pgvector | PostgreSQL 17 | Catalog, ontology, app data, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Connection credential storage | n/a | Keep ports 3001 and 3002 on a private network. FastAPI trusts the user identity the frontend forwards in the `x-auto-ontology-user-id` header, and the ingestion service's endpoints (ingest, delete, reset, compile) have no authentication of their own. Browser and API clients go through the web app on port 3000, and MCP clients through the MCP server on port 3003. ## Use it from your agent ### MCP server The [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server gives any MCP client read-only tools over the ontology. Each user signs in through Auto-Ontology, and every call runs with that user's permissions. | Job | Tools | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | Readiness | `check_readiness`: can this deployment answer anything at all | | Terms | `search_terms`, `get_term`, `get_term_columns`, `get_term_sql_attributes`, `get_sql_attribute`, `describe_table` | | Answerability | `check_answerable`: does the ontology cover this question | | Questions | `ask_question`: the answer, the SQL, and the rows | Run the server against your deployment: ```bash AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \ uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp ``` Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "auto-ontology": { "url": "http://l
